title: Non-pressure ulcer depth and burn extent
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the ulcer, or for the burn extent (T31) when the note is about a burn (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up of a chronic wound on the right heel.

HPI
The patient is a 77-year-old woman who presents today for a scheduled evaluation of a chronic ulcer located on her right heel. She reports that the wound has persisted for several months and she has noticed increasing pain and a change in the appearance of the site. She denies any recent trauma to the area or acute fevers. She notes that she has been managing the wound with home dressings, but the area has not shown significant improvement in size or healing. She reports some difficulty with mobility due to discomfort.

Medication List
- Lisinopril 10 mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20 mg daily
- Amlodipine 5 mg daily

Vitals
Blood Pressure: 138/82 mmHg
Heart Rate: 74 bpm
Temperature: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on room air
Weight: 154 lbs

Recent Labs
WBC: 8.2 x 10^9/L
Hemoglobin: 12.4 g/dL
eGFR: 68 mL/min/1.73m2
Glucose: 118 mg/dL

Review of Systems
The patient reports no recent fevers, chills, or night sweats. She denies any new shortness of breath or chest pain. She reports localized pain at the site of the wound but denies systemic symptoms. No reports of vision changes or urinary symptoms.

Social History
The patient resides in a single-story home with her spouse. She is a retired school teacher. She denies current tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History
Mother had hypertension. Father had a history of hyperlipidemia.

Exam
General: The patient is a well-appearing, alert, and oriented 77-year-old female in no acute distress.
Skin/Musculoskeletal: On examination of the right heel, there is a chronic ulcer measuring approximately 3 cm in diameter. The wound bed shows significant necrotic tissue. Deep palpation and visualization reveal evidence of necrosis of bone underlying the wound. The surrounding skin is erythematous and indurated. No drainage is noted at this time.

Assessment
1. Chronic ulcer of the right heel with necrosis of bone.

Plan
The patient will be scheduled for a surgical debridement of the right heel to remove the necrotic tissue and address the involvement of the bone. She was instructed to keep the area clean and dry until the procedure. She will be monitored for signs of worsening infection.

Electronically signed,
E. Castillo, DO
May 14, 2026
explanations: Non-pressure chronic ulcer of right heel and midfoot with necrosis of bone: L97.414 (HCC 380).

hccs.label: Chronic Ulcer of Skin/Except Pressure/Through to Bone or Muscle
